questions.q: Jaipal Singh Munda is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.solution:

Key Points

• Jaipal Singh Munda was an Indian politician, writer, and a member of the Constituent Assembly of India.

• Besides his sports career, he was an influential tribal leader and played a significant role in advocating for the rights of indigenous people in India.

Additional Information

• Field hockey is a team sport played on grass or artificial turf, with teams aiming to score goals by hitting a ball into the opposing team's net using hockey sticks.

• It is a popular sport worldwide, particularly in countries like India, Australia, Germany, and the Netherlands.

• Field hockey is governed by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), which organizes various international competitions, including the Hockey World Cup and the Hockey Champions Trophy.

• India has a rich history in field hockey, with the national team having won multiple Olympic gold medals, especially during the mid-20th century.

• Olympic Games:

• The Olympics are a leading international sporting event featuring summer and winter sports competitions in which thousands of athletes from around the world participate in various competitions.

• The Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating by occurring every two years.

• The modern Olympic Games were first held in 1896 in Athens, Greece, and have since grown to become the world's foremost sports competition.

• The Olympics aim to promote peace and unity among nations through sports and celebrate athletic excellence.

• Jaipal Singh Munda's Legacy:

• Jaipal Singh Munda is remembered not only for his sporting achievements but also for his significant contributions to Indian politics and society.

• He was a prominent tribal leader and a key figure in advocating for the rights and welfare of indigenous communities in India.

• As a member of the Constituent Assembly, he played an important role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution, particularly in the context of protecting the rights of tribal people.

• His legacy continues to inspire many in the fields of sports, politics, and social justice.

• The Gandharva Mahavidyalaya continues to be a prominent institution for music education in India.

• His efforts in music education laid the foundation for many future musicians and music educators in India.

questions.q: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 24.

Key Points

• Article 24 of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment.

• This Article is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, which aims to protect children from exploitation.

• It was introduced to safeguard children from engaging in work that can be detrimental to their health, safety, and development.

• Violation of this Article can lead to legal consequences and penalties as per the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.

Additional Information

• Article 23:

• Prohibits human trafficking and forced labor.

• It states that traffic in human beings, begar (forced labor), and other similar forms of forced labor are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law.

• Article 25:

• Guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.

• It provides all individuals the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate their religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.

• Article 26:

• Provides freedom to manage religious affairs.

• It gives every religious denomination or any section thereof the right to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage its own affairs in matters of religion, own and acquire movable and immovable property, and administer such property in accordance with the law.

• Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986:

• This Act prohibits the engagement of children in certain employments and regulates the conditions of work of children in other employments.

• The Act defines a child as a person who has not completed 14 years of age.

• It lays down a detailed framework for the prohibition and regulation of child labor in India.

questions.q: Bihu festival is the main festival of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Assam.

Key Points

• Bihu is the main festival of Assam, celebrated with great joy and enthusiasm.

• There are three major Bihu festivals in Assam: Bohag Bihu (or Rongali Bihu), Kati Bihu (or Kongali Bihu), and Magh Bihu (or Bhogali Bihu).

• Bihu marks the harvest season and is closely related to the agricultural calendar of Assam.

• It is a non-religious festival and is celebrated by all communities irrespective of their religion, caste, or creed.

Additional Information

• Bohag Bihu (Rongali Bihu)

• It is celebrated in mid-April and marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year.

• Bohag Bihu is the most popular Bihu, characterized by feasts, music, and dancing.

• People wear traditional attire and perform the Bihu dance, showcasing their cultural heritage.

• Kati Bihu (Kongali Bihu)

• It is celebrated in mid-October and is a more subdued festival compared to Bohag Bihu.

• Kati Bihu is associated with the sowing of crops and is marked by lighting earthen lamps in paddy fields and praying for a good harvest.

• It is a time of introspection and prayer for the welfare of the crops.

• Magh Bihu (Bhogali Bihu)

• It is celebrated in mid-January and marks the end of the harvest season.

• Magh Bihu is characterized by feasts and bonfires, where people gather to celebrate the bounty of the harvest.

• Traditional games such as buffalo fighting and pot-breaking are also part of the celebrations.

questions.q: As per article 158, the Governor shall NOT be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in _ Schedule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is First.

Key Points

• According to Article 158 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor of a State shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in the First Schedule.

• The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the states and union territories of India.

• This provision ensures the independence of the Governor's office from legislative influence.

• The Governor must resign from any legislative positions before assuming office to maintain this separation of powers.

Additional Information

• Article 158

• Article 158 of the Constitution of India pertains to the conditions of the Governor's office.

• Clause (1) of Article 158 states that the Governor shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State specified in the First Schedule.

• This clause ensures that the Governor remains unbiased and can execute his/her duties without any legislative pressures.

• First Schedule

• The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution details the list of States and Union Territories along with their respective territories.

• It provides the official names of the States and Union Territories and their territorial boundaries.

• Role of the Governor

• The Governor is the Constitutional head of a state in India.

• He/she is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.

• The Governor's role includes giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, appointing the Chief Minister, and ensuring the state administration is carried out according to the Constitution.

questions.q: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Cheilosis.

Key Points

• Cheilosis, also known as angular cheilitis, is an inflammatory condition that affects the corners of the mouth.

• It is characterized by the formation of cracks, crusting, and scaling at the mouth corners.

• Cheilosis is commonly caused by a deficiency in Vitamin B2 (riboflavin).

• Other contributing factors can include fungal infections and poor oral hygiene.

Additional Information

• Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)

• Riboflavin is a water-soluble vitamin that is essential for energy production and cellular function.

• It helps in the metabolism of fats, drugs, and steroids and is crucial for the conversion of carbohydrates into ATP (adenosine triphosphate).

• Deficiency in riboflavin can lead to symptoms such as sore throat, redness and swelling of the lining of the mouth and throat, and cheilosis.

• Psoriasis

• Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that causes the rapid buildup of skin cells.

• This buildup of cells causes scaling on the skin’s surface.

• Inflammation and redness around the scales are fairly common.

• Urticaria (Hives)

• Urticaria, commonly known as hives, is a skin reaction that causes itchy welts.

• It is usually caused by an allergic reaction to food, medicine, or other irritants.

• Atopic Dermatitis

• Atopic dermatitis, also known as eczema, is a condition that makes the skin red and itchy.

• It is common in children but can occur at any age.

• Atopic dermatitis is long-lasting (chronic) and tends to flare periodically.

questions.q: Which of the following Delhi sultans introduced two coins, namely silver tanka and copper jital?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Iltutmish.

Key Points

• Iltutmish was the third ruler of the Delhi Sultanate and the founder of the Shamsi dynasty.

• He introduced the silver tanka and the copper jital coins, which became the standard currency of the Delhi Sultanate.

• The silver tanka weighed 175 grains and was the first regular currency introduced in India by the Delhi Sultanate.

• His coinage system helped to stabilize the economy and provided a reliable medium of exchange for trade and commerce.

Additional Information

• Delhi Sultanate:

• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent for 320 years (1206–1526).

• The Sultanate is noted for its integration of the Indian subcontinent into the Muslim world and its role in the spread of Islam in South Asia.

• Silver Tanka:

• The silver tanka was a high-value coin made of silver and used for large transactions.

• It had a standard weight of 175 grains (approximately 11.3 grams).

• The introduction of the silver tanka standardized the monetary system and facilitated trade.

• Copper Jital:

• The copper jital was a lower value coin made of copper and used for smaller transactions.

• It complemented the silver tanka and provided a comprehensive monetary system covering both high and low-value transactions.

• The copper jital played a significant role in the everyday economy of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Economic Impact:

• The introduction of these coins by Iltutmish helped to stabilize the economy of the Delhi Sultanate.

• It provided a reliable and standardized medium of exchange, which was crucial for trade and commerce.

• This monetary reform was an important step in the consolidation of the Delhi Sultanate's power and its administration.

questions.q: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7.

Key Points

• India's first Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on the agricultural sector.

• From 1947 to 1990, a total of 7 Five-Year Plans were successfully completed in India.

• The Five-Year Plans aimed at economic development through various sectors like agriculture, industry, and services.

• The seventh Five-Year Plan ended in 1990, marking the completion of 7 such plans within the specified period.

Additional Information

• Five-Year Plans in India

• The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.

• They were modeled after the Soviet Union's centralized economic planning, aiming to promote rapid industrialization and economic development.

• Each plan was formulated, executed, and monitored by the Planning Commission of India, which was established in 1950.

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on the agricultural sector, aiming to overcome food shortages and improve living standards.

• Planning Commission

• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.

• It was established in 1950 by a Cabinet resolution under the advice of the first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The Commission was tasked with assessing the country's resources and formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources.

• In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) by the Narendra Modi government.

• Objectives of the Five-Year Plans

• The primary objectives were to increase national income, achieve full employment, reduce inequalities of income and wealth, and establish a socialist pattern of society.

• Other specific objectives included reducing poverty, improving infrastructure, and enhancing the quality of life for Indian citizens.

• Significance of the Five-Year Plans

• The Five-Year Plans were instrumental in transforming India's economy from an agrarian base to a more diversified one with a substantial industrial sector.

• They laid the foundation for modern economic development and contributed to significant improvements in various economic indicators, such as GDP growth and poverty reduction.

• The plans also played a critical role in establishing and expanding public sector enterprises and infrastructure development across the country.

questions.q: Name the straight chain alkane having chemical formula C₉H₂₀, which is used as a research chemical and in making biodegradable detergents.
questions.solution:

Key Points

• Nonane is an alkane with the chemical formula C9H20.

• It is a straight-chain hydrocarbon.

• Nonane is commonly used as a research chemical.

• It plays a role in making biodegradable detergents.

Additional Information

• Alkanes

• Alkanes, also known as paraffins, are hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.

• They are saturated hydrocarbons, meaning they contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.

• Alkanes are relatively non-reactive and are primarily used as fuels and solvents.

• The simplest alkane is methane (CH4), and the series continues with ethane (C2H6), propane (C3H8), etc.

• Biodegradable Detergents

• Biodegradable detergents are formulated to break down and decompose naturally, reducing environmental impact.

• They are designed to be more eco-friendly and less harmful to aquatic life.

• These detergents often use surfactants derived from natural sources rather than synthetic chemicals.

• Nonane can be used in the production of such surfactants due to its properties.

• Research Chemicals

• Research chemicals are compounds used by scientists for medical and scientific research purposes.

• They are not intended for human or veterinary use.

• These chemicals help in the study of chemical reactions, biological processes, and the development of new materials.

• Proper handling and ethical considerations are crucial when working with research chemicals.

questions.q: When you take Lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube and heat it, you will observe the emission of brown fumes that are of _.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nitrogen dioxide.

Key Points

• Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is a brown gas that is emitted when lead nitrate is heated.

• Lead nitrate decomposes to form lead oxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), and oxygen (O₂).

• The chemical reaction for this process is:

2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂.

• The brown fumes observed during the heating of lead nitrate are characteristic of nitrogen dioxide.

Additional Information

• Lead Nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂):

• It is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Pb(NO₃)₂.

• It is soluble in water and is commonly used in laboratories and industries.

• When heated, lead nitrate decomposes into lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen.

• Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂):

• It is a reddish-brown gas with a characteristic sharp, biting odor.

• It is one of several nitrogen oxides and is a significant air pollutant.

• NO₂ is a major component of smog and can have harmful effects on the respiratory system.

• Chemical Reactions:

• In chemistry, a chemical reaction is a process that leads to the transformation of one set of chemical substances to another.

• Reactions involve the breaking of bonds in reactants and the formation of new bonds in products.

• Decomposition reactions, like the heating of lead nitrate, involve the breakdown of a single compound into two or more simpler substances.

questions.q: Who among the following sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?

Key Points

• Seleucus I Nicator was one of the generals of Alexander the Great and a founding ruler of the Seleucid Empire.

• He sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

• Megasthenes authored the work Indika, which provides valuable insights into the Mauryan Empire and Indian society.

• The diplomatic mission symbolized the friendly relations and the exchange of cultural and political ideas between the Seleucid Empire and the Mauryan Empire.

Additional Information

• Seleucus I Nicator

• He was born in 358 BCE and died in 281 BCE.

• He played a crucial role in the Wars of the Diadochi that followed Alexander's death.

• He established the Seleucid Empire, which at its height included regions of the eastern Mediterranean, the Middle East, and parts of Asia.

• Seleucus was known for founding several cities, including Antioch and Seleucia.

• Megasthenes

• He was a Greek historian and diplomat.

• His work "Indika" is one of the earliest Western accounts of India.

• Megasthenes' observations covered various aspects of Indian society, including its geography, social structure, economy, and administration.

• Despite some inaccuracies, his accounts remain a significant historical source.

• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire in ancient India.

• Chandragupta ruled from 321 BCE to 297 BCE.

• He is known for unifying the Indian subcontinent and establishing a centralized government.

questions.q: Which of the following states is one of those states that have no Panchayati Raj Institution at all?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

Key Points

• Nagaland does not have Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) due to its unique traditional and customary laws.

• The Nagaland Village and Area Councils Act, 1978 governs local governance in the state instead of the Panchayati Raj system.

• The Constitution (Seventy-Third Amendment) Act, 1992, which introduced the Panchayati Raj system in India, does not apply to Nagaland.

• Nagaland's traditional village councils and customary practices are protected under Article 371(A) of the Indian Constitution.

Additional Information

• Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)

• Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) are a system of rural local self-government in India.

• The system was institutionalized through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

• This act provides a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of over 2 million, consisting of:

• Gram Panchayat at the village level

• Panchayat Samiti at the intermediate level

• Zila Parishad at the district level

• The objective of PRIs is to ensure democracy at the grassroots level and empower rural India.

• Article 371(A)

• Article 371(A) of the Indian Constitution provides special provisions with respect to the state of Nagaland.

• It ensures that no act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices, Naga customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law, ownership and transfer of land and its resources shall apply to Nagaland unless the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland by a resolution so decides.

• This article preserves the unique social and cultural practices of Nagaland.

• Nagaland Village and Area Councils Act, 1978

• This act provides for the establishment of village councils in Nagaland.

• Village councils are responsible for administration, development, and maintaining law and order in villages.

• The members of the village councils are selected according to the traditional customs and practices of the Naga tribes.

• This act ensures that local governance in Nagaland respects and incorporates the traditional and customary laws of the Naga people.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of capital receipts?
options: Revenue from the sale of government assets
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Revenue from the sale of government assets.

Key Points

• Capital receipts are funds received by the government that create a liability or reduce financial assets.

• Revenue from the sale of government assets is considered a capital receipt because it involves the sale of existing government assets, which reduces the financial assets of the government.

• Examples of capital receipts include loans raised by the government, disinvestment proceeds, and borrowings from international organizations.

• Capital receipts do not occur regularly and are usually non-recurring in nature.

Additional Information

• Revenue Receipts:

• These are funds received by the government which do not create any liability or reduce any financial asset.

• Examples include taxes, interest receipts, and dividends and profits from public sector enterprises.

• Revenue receipts are regular and recurring in nature.

• Taxes on Income:

• Taxes collected from individuals and corporations based on their income.

• These fall under the category of revenue receipts.

• Interest on Government Bonds:

• This is the interest income earned by the government from the bonds it has issued.

• It is also considered a revenue receipt.

• Grants-in-aid:

• These are funds provided by one government to another, typically for a specific purpose.

• Grants-in-aid are considered revenue receipts.

• Drain of Wealth Theory

• The "Drain of Wealth" theory proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji argued that Britain was systematically transferring Indian wealth to Britain.

• This theory was primarily articulated through his writings and speeches, particularly in his seminal work "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".

• Economic Nationalism

• Economic nationalism is a body of policies that emphasize domestic control of the economy, labor, and capital formation, often advocating protectionism and import substitution.

• Dadabhai Naoroji's critique of British economic policies laid the foundation for economic nationalism in India, influencing the Swadeshi movement and later economic policies post-independence.

questions.q: In which month is the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) located around 20°N-25°N latitude (over the Gangetic plain)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is July.

Key Points

• The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a region that circles the Earth, near the equator, where the trade winds of the Northern and Southern Hemispheres come together.

• In the summer months, particularly in July, the ITCZ shifts northwards to around 20ºN-25ºN latitude, which is over the Gangetic plain in India.

• This northward shift is due to the intense solar heating of the landmass, which creates low pressure areas that draw the ITCZ northwards.

• The movement of the ITCZ is significant as it influences the monsoon patterns, bringing heavy rains to the Indian subcontinent during this period.

Additional Information

• Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)

• The ITCZ is also known as the Equatorial Convergence Zone or the Doldrums.

• It is characterized by convective activity which generates often vigorous thunderstorms over large areas.

• The position of the ITCZ varies seasonally, moving northwards during the Northern Hemisphere summer and southwards during the Southern Hemisphere summer.

• The ITCZ plays a crucial role in the global climate system and is a key component of the monsoon systems in tropical regions.

• Monsoon

• The monsoon is a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding changes in precipitation.

• In South Asia, the summer monsoon brings heavy rainfall, which is vital for agriculture but can also lead to floods.

• The monsoon is driven by the differential heating of land and sea, with the ITCZ acting as a major component in its formation and movement.

• The onset and intensity of the monsoon are closely monitored by meteorologists to predict weather patterns and prepare for agricultural planning.

• Gangetic Plain

• The Gangetic Plain is a large and fertile plain encompassing most of northern and eastern India, parts of Pakistan, and Bangladesh.

• It is formed by the sediment deposits of the Ganges and its tributaries.

• The plain is one of the most densely populated regions in the world and is crucial for India's agriculture.

• The northward shift of the ITCZ during summer months significantly impacts the rainfall distribution in this region.

questions.q: The ratio of expenditure to savings of a woman is 4 : 1. If her income and expenditure are increased by 20% and 10%, respectively, then find the percentage change in her savings.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the weighted average / net deviation method:

Overall % change = [(Exp Ratio × Exp % Change) + (Sav Ratio × Sav % Change)] ÷ Total Ratio

20% = [(4 × 10%) + (1 × x%)] ÷ (4 + 1)

100% = 40% + x% ⇒ x = 60%

∴ The correct answer is 60%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = 4 : 1

Increase in Income = 20%

Increase in Expenditure = 10%

Formula Used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100%



Calculations:

⇒ Let the savings be 100 units.

⇒ Then, expenditure = 4 × 100 = 400 units.

⇒ Initial Income = 400 + 100 = 500 units.

⇒ New Income = 500 + (20% of 500) = 500 + 100 = 600 units.

⇒ New Expenditure = 400 + (10% of 400) = 400 + 40 = 440 units.

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = 600 − 440 = 160 units.

⇒ Increase in savings = 160 − 100 = 60 units.

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (60 ÷ 100) × 100% = 60%.

∴ The correct answer is 60%.

Additional Information

Income and Expenditure relation

Income is always the sum of expenditure and savings (I = E + S). Any change in income must be balanced by combined changes in expenditure and savings.

Weighted Average Method

When a quantity is divided into parts, the overall percentage change is the weighted average of the percentage changes of its parts: Overall % = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Alligation Method

The rule of alligation can also be applied to find the ratio of parts or the change in one part if the overall change and the change in the other part are known.

questions.q: A man loses 28% by selling an article for ₹144. If he sells it for ₹288, what will be his gain/loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Selling price ₹144 corresponds to a 28% loss, which means it is 72% of CP.

The equivalent percentage for ₹288 = (72 / 144) × 288 = 144% of CP.

Since the equivalent value is greater than 100%, there is a profit.

Gain percentage = 144% − 100% = 44%.

∴ The correct answer is Gain, 44%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Loss percentage = 28%

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹144

New Selling Price (SP₂) = ₹288

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) / (100 − Loss%)

Gain% = (Gain / CP) × 100



Calculations:

⇒ CP = (144 × 100) / (100 − 28)

⇒ CP = 14400 / 72 = ₹200

⇒ New SP = ₹288

⇒ Gain = New SP − CP = 288 − 200 = ₹88

⇒ Gain% = (88 / 200) × 100 = 44%

∴ The correct answer is Gain, 44%.

Additional Information

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Final selling price is SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: (a + b − (a × b) / 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

A dealer who claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight makes a profit %. The formula is: Profit % = (Error / (True Value − Error)) × 100.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the cylindrical tank, r = 14 cm

Volume of water drawn out, V = 616 litres

Formula Used:

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

1 Litre = 1000 cm³

⇒ 616000 = 616 × h

⇒ h = 616000 ÷ 616

⇒ h = 1000 cm

Additional Information

Cylinder Formulas

Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh | Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r+h).

Volume Conversions

1 Litre = 1000 cm³ | 1 m³ = 1000 Litres | 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³.

Direct Proportion in Cylinders

For a uniform cross-section tank, the volume drawn or added is directly proportional to the change in height (ΔV = Base Area × Δh).

questions.q: Find the diameter (in cm) of a circle whose circumference is equal to the sum of the circumferences of two circles of radii 12 cm and 16 cm.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the circumference of a circle equals the sum of the circumferences of two other circles, its radius is the sum of their radii.

⇒ New Radius (R) = r₁ + r₂

⇒ R = 12 + 16 = 28 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2 × 28 = 56 cm

∴ The correct answer is 56 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the first circle (r₁) = 12 cm

Radius of the second circle (r₂) = 16 cm

Formula Used:

Circumference of a circle (C) = 2πr

Diameter of a circle (D) = 2 × r



Calculations:

Let the radius of the newly formed circle be R.

⇒ Circumference of the new circle = Sum of the circumferences of the smaller circles

⇒ 2πR = 2πr₁ + 2πr₂

⇒ 2πR = 2π(r₁ + r₂)

⇒ R = r₁ + r₂

⇒ R = 12 + 16 = 28 cm

Now, calculate the diameter of the larger circle:

⇒ D = 2 × R

⇒ D = 2 × 28 = 56 cm

∴ The correct answer is 56 cm.

Additional Information

Sum of Circumferences vs Radii

Since the circumference is directly proportional to the radius (C = 2πr), adding the circumferences of two circles yields a new circle whose radius is linearly equal to the sum of their individual radii: R = r₁ + r₂.

Sum of Areas vs Radii

When the area of a circle equals the sum of the areas of two other circles, the relationship between their radii becomes R² = r₁² + r₂², which perfectly aligns with the Pythagorean theorem.

Diameter and Circumference

The circumference can also be expressed directly as C = π × D. This mathematical definition implies that the ratio of any circle's circumference to its diameter is always the constant value π (≈ 3.14159).

Area of a Kite

The area of a kite is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

questions.q: The relation between K1 and K₂ for which the system of linear equations K₁x + 3y = 8 and 4x + K₂y = 16 represents coincident lines, is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two lines to be coincident, the ratio of all their corresponding coefficients must be equal.

⇒ a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

⇒ K₁/4 = 3/K₂ = 8/16 = 1/2

⇒ K₁ = 4 × (1/2) = 2

⇒ K₂ = 3 ÷ (1/2) = 6

Checking the options, 6 = 3 × 2 clearly satisfies K₂ = 3K₁.

∴ The correct answer is K₂ = 3K₁.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: K₁x + 3y = 8

Equation 2: 4x + K₂y = 16

Formula Used:

For two linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ to represent coincident lines, the condition is:

a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂

Calculations:

⇒ Comparing the given equations with standard forms, we get:

⇒ a₁ = K₁, b₁ = 3, c₁ = 8

⇒ a₂ = 4, b₂ = K₂, c₂ = 16

⇒ Applying the condition for coincident lines:

⇒ K₁/4 = 3/K₂ = 8/16

⇒ 8/16 can be simplified to 1/2

⇒ K₁/4 = 1/2 ⇒ K₁ = 2

⇒ 3/K₂ = 1/2 ⇒ K₂ = 6

⇒ Now substitute K₁ = 2 and K₂ = 6 into the given options:

⇒ Option 1: K₂ = 3K₁ ⇒ 6 = 3 × 2 ⇒ 6 = 6 (Satisfies condition)

⇒ Option 2: K₂ + 3K₁ = 0 ⇒ 6 + 6 = 12 ≠ 0 (Does not satisfy condition)

∴ The correct answer is K₂ = 3K₁.

Additional Information

Condition for Intersecting Lines (Unique Solution)

For two linear equations a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂ to intersect at exactly one point and have a unique solution, the condition is a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.

Condition for Parallel Lines (No Solution)

For the lines to be strictly parallel with no common points, the condition is a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.

Condition for Coincident Lines (Infinite Solutions)

For the lines to overlap completely and represent the exact same line with infinite solutions, the ratio of all coefficients must be strictly equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

questions.q: Naman borrows a sum of ₹3,48,020 at the rate of 8% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹15,090 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Naman clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial P = ₹3,48,020; Remaining P after repayment = 3,48,020 − 15,090 = ₹3,32,930.

SI for 1st year = 8% of 3,48,020 = ₹27,841.6.

SI for 2nd year = 8% of 3,32,930 = ₹26,634.4.

Total amount due at 2nd year end = Remaining P + SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ 3,32,930 + 27,841.6 + 26,634.4 = ₹3,87,406.

∴ The correct answer is ₹3,87,406.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Principal (P) = ₹3,48,020

Rate of Interest (R) = 8% per annum

Principal repaid at the end of 1st year = ₹15,090

Formula Used:

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100



Calculation:

⇒ Interest for the 1st year (I₁) = (3,48,020 × 8 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹27,841.60

⇒ Remaining principal for the 2nd year (P₂) = 3,48,020 − 15,090 = ₹3,32,930

⇒ Interest for the 2nd year (I₂) = (3,32,930 × 8 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹26,634.40

⇒ Total amount due at the end of the 2nd year = Remaining Principal + I₁ + I₂

⇒ Total amount = 3,32,930 + 27,841.60 + 26,634.40 = ₹3,87,406

∴ The correct answer is ₹3,87,406.

Additional Information

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated exclusively on the principal amount for each period. The accrued interest does not generate further interest. Formula: I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Partial Principal Repayment

When a portion of the principal is repaid midway, the new principal for calculating subsequent simple interest is reduced by the repayment amount. The unpaid accrued interest is kept aside and does not affect the new principal.

Total Due Amount

To clear all dues at the end of the tenure, the borrower must pay the remaining principal along with the sum of interest accrued across all individual time periods.

questions.q:
If x = p sec A cos B , y = q sec A sin B and z = r tan A , what is the value of the following expression?

p2x2​ + q2y2​ - r2z2​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put standard angles A = 0° and B = 0° to quickly solve the expression.

⇒ x = p(1)(1) = p, y = q(1)(0) = 0, and z = r(0) = 0

Substitute these calculated values into the expression (x² / p²) + (y² / q²) − (z² / r²):

⇒ (p² / p²) + 0 − 0 = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ x = p sec A cos B

⇒ y = q sec A sin B

⇒ z = r tan A

Formula Used:

⇒ sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

⇒ sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

Calculations:

Rearranging the given equations, we get:

⇒ x / p = sec A cos B

⇒ y / q = sec A sin B

⇒ z / r = tan A

Substitute these values into the required expression:

⇒ (x² / p²) + (y² / q²) − (z² / r²)

⇒ (sec A cos B)² + (sec A sin B)² − (tan A)²

⇒ sec² A cos² B + sec² A sin² B − tan² A

Taking sec² A common from the first two terms:

⇒ sec² A (cos² B + sin² B) − tan² A

Using the identity cos² B + sin² B = 1:

⇒ sec² A (1) − tan² A

⇒ sec² A − tan² A

Using the identity sec² A − tan² A = 1:

⇒ 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Identities

These fundamental relations form the basis of trigonometric simplifications: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Value Substitution Method

For pure variable trigonometric expressions, substituting standard angles (like 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°) provides the fastest route to the solution by avoiding complex expansions.

Trigonometric Ratios at 0°

At an angle of 0°, sin 0° = 0, cos 0° = 1, tan 0° = 0, and sec 0° = 1. These specific values are extremely helpful in eliminating terms rapidly from algebraic-trigonometric equations.

questions.q: The value of (x + y)² + (x - y)² is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Directly apply the standard algebraic identity:

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)

Substitute a = x and b = y in the formula:

(x + y)² + (x − y)² = 2(x² + y²)

∴ The correct answer is 2(x² + y²).

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (x + y)² + (x − y)²

Formula Used:

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

Calculations:

⇒ Expanding the first term: (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

⇒ Expanding the second term: (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy

⇒ Adding both the expanded terms together:

⇒ (x² + y² + 2xy) + (x² + y² − 2xy)

⇒ Group the like terms together:

⇒ x² + x² + y² + y² + 2xy − 2xy

⇒ The + 2xy and − 2xy cancel each other out.

⇒ 2x² + 2y²

⇒ Taking 2 common from both the terms:

⇒ 2(x² + y²)

∴ The correct answer is 2(x² + y²).

Additional Information

Difference of Perfect Squares

When the perfect squares are subtracted instead of added, the identity becomes: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Difference of Squares

The difference between two squared terms factors into the product of the sum and difference of the base terms: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Sum and Difference of Cubes

For sum of cubes: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). For difference of cubes: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Square of Trinomial

The expansion of three combined terms squared is given by: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca.

questions.q: A policeman noticed a thief at some distance. The policeman started running to catch the thief and the thief also started running at the same time. The speed of both policeman and the thief was 12 km per hour and 10 km per hour, respectively. It took 30 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the initial distance (in metres) between them.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When running in the same direction, Relative Speed = SP − ST.

Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

Time = 30 minutes = 1/2 hour

Initial distance = Relative speed × Time = 2 × 1/2 = 1 km

Convert to metres: 1 km = 1000 m

∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of policeman (SP) = 12 km/h

Speed of thief (ST) = 10 km/h

Time taken to catch the thief (t) = 30 minutes = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 hours

Formula Used:

Relative speed (same direction) = SP − ST

Distance = Speed × Time



Calculation:

⇒ The policeman and the thief run in the same direction, so we calculate their relative speed.

⇒ Relative speed = 12 − 10 = 2 km/h

⇒ Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time taken to catch

⇒ Initial Distance = 2 km/h × 0.5 hours

⇒ Initial Distance = 1 km

⇒ Convert kilometers to meters: 1 km = 1000 m

∴ The correct answer is 1000 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions towards each other, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversions for Speed and Distance

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Always ensure units match before applying distance formulas.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

questions.q: If m is even, then 8m - 1 is divisible by:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put the smallest even number for m, i.e., m = 2.

⇒ 8m − 1 = 8² − 1

⇒ 64 − 1 = 63

Checking the given options, 63 is perfectly divisible by 63.

∴ The correct answer is 63.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = 8m − 1

m is an even natural number.

Formula Used:

xⁿ − yⁿ is completely divisible by (x − y) for all natural numbers n.

Calculations:

Since m is even, let m = 2k, where k is a natural number (k = 1, 2, 3, ...).

⇒ 8m − 1 = 8²k − 1

⇒ (8²)k − 1k

⇒ 64k − 1k

Comparing this with xⁿ − yⁿ:

⇒ 64k − 1k is completely divisible by (64 − 1).

⇒ 64 − 1 = 63

Hence, the given expression will always be divisible by 63 for any even value of m.

∴ The correct answer is 63.

Additional Information

Divisibility of xⁿ − yⁿ

It is always divisible by (x − y) for all natural numbers n. If n is an even number, it is also divisible by (x + y).

Divisibility of xⁿ + yⁿ

It is divisible by (x + y) only when n is an odd natural number. It is never completely divisible by (x − y).

Unit Digit of 8m

The unit digit of powers of 8 follows a cyclicity of 4: 8, 4, 2, 6. For even powers, the unit digit is either 4 or 6.

questions.q: Find the value of 'k' for which the system of equations 4x + 6y = 7 and 6x + (k + 4)y - 21 = 0 has a unique solution.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a system of linear equations to have a unique solution, the ratio of their x-coefficients must not be equal to the ratio of their y-coefficients.

4 / 6 ≠ 6 / (k + 4)

2 / 3 ≠ 6 / (k + 4)

2(k + 4) ≠ 18 ⇒ k + 4 ≠ 9

k ≠ 5

∴ The correct answer is k ≠ 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: 4x + 6y − 7 = 0

Equation 2: 6x + (k + 4)y − 21 = 0

Formula Used:

For a system of linear equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to have a unique solution, the condition is:

a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂

Calculations:

⇒ a₁ = 4, b₁ = 6

⇒ a₂ = 6, b₂ = k + 4

Applying the unique solution condition:

⇒ 4 / 6 ≠ 6 / (k + 4)

Simplifying the fraction on the left side:

⇒ 2 / 3 ≠ 6 / (k + 4)

Cross multiplying to solve for k:

⇒ 2 × (k + 4) ≠ 6 × 3

⇒ 2k + 8 ≠ 18

⇒ 2k ≠ 18 − 8

⇒ 2k ≠ 10

⇒ k ≠ 5

∴ The correct answer is k ≠ 5.

Additional Information

Unique Solution (Intersecting Lines)

A system has a unique solution if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂. The lines intersect at exactly one point, making them consistent.

Infinite Solutions (Coincident Lines)

A system has infinitely many solutions if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. The lines overlap exactly and are dependent.

No Solution (Parallel Lines)

A system has no solution if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂. The lines are strictly parallel and never intersect.

questions.q: In the 8th class, consisting of 30 students, a Mathematics test was taken. 10 students had an average score of 90. The other students had an average score of 75. What is the average score of the whole class?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the base average be 75.

Deviation for 10 students = 90 − 75 = +15

Total deviation for these 10 students = 10 × 15 = +150

Average deviation for all 30 students = +150 ÷ 30 = +5

Overall average = Base average + Average deviation = 75 + 5 = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of students in the class = 30

Number of students with an average score of 90 = 10

Number of remaining students = 30 − 10 = 20

Average score of the remaining 20 students = 75

Formula Used:

Average = Sum of all scores ÷ Total number of students

20 Students

Sum: 1500

Total: 30 Students
Combined Avg: (900 + 1500) ÷ 30 = 80

Calculations:

⇒ Total score of the first 10 students = 10 × 90 = 900

⇒ Total score of the remaining 20 students = 20 × 75 = 1500

⇒ Total score of all 30 students = 900 + 1500 = 2400

⇒ Average score of the whole class = 2400 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80.

Additional Information

Weighted Average

When combining multiple groups, the formula for the total average is A = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the number of elements and A is the average of each respective group.

Net Deviation Method

By assuming a base average, one can easily find the overall average by calculating the net positive or negative deviation and distributing it equally among all components. It speeds up calculations remarkably.

Alligation Method

Averages can also be calculated using mixtures and alligations rules where the ratio of quantities (n₁ : n₂) equals the inverse ratio of the difference between group averages and the combined average.

Since 72° − 27° = 45°, we use the identity tan(A − B) = (tan A − tan B) / (1 + tan A × tan B).

⇒ tan(72° − 27°) = (tan 72° − tan 27°) / (1 + tan 72° × tan 27°)

⇒ tan 45° = (tan 72° − tan 27°) / (1 + tan 72° × tan 27°)

⇒ 1 = (tan 72° − tan 27°) / (1 + tan 72° × tan 27°)

⇒ 1 + tan 72° × tan 27° = tan 72° − tan 27°

⇒ tan 72° − tan 27° − tan 72° × tan 27° = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Expression: tan 72° − tan 27° − tan 72° × tan 27°

⇒ 1 + tan 72° × tan 27° = tan 72° − tan 27°

⇒ tan 72° − tan 27° − tan 72° × tan 27° = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

questions.q: If A : B = 6 : 8 and B : C = 5 : 11, then A : B : C is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Reverse 'N' multiplication method for combined ratios:

A : B = 6 : 8 → Simplifies to 3 : 4

B : C = 5 : 11

Multiply vertically and diagonally:

A : B : C = (3 × 5) : (4 × 5) : (4 × 11)

∴ The correct answer is 15 : 20 : 44.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of A : B = 6 : 8

Ratio of B : C = 5 : 11



Calculations:

⇒ First, simplify the ratio A : B

⇒ A : B = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4

⇒ The given ratio B : C = 5 : 11

⇒ To combine them, make the common term (B) equal in both ratios.

⇒ LCM of the B terms (4 and 5) is 20.

⇒ Multiply A : B by 5 → (3 × 5) : (4 × 5) = 15 : 20

⇒ Multiply B : C by 4 → (5 × 4) : (11 × 4) = 20 : 44

⇒ Now, B is equal (20) in both ratios.

⇒ Therefore, combined ratio A : B : C = 15 : 20 : 44

∴ The correct answer is 15 : 20 : 44.

Additional Information

Combining Ratios

To combine A : B and B : C into A : B : C, find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the values representing B, then scale both ratios to make B equal in both.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are given, the ratio of the product of their antecedents to the product of their consequents is called the compound ratio. For a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is ac : bd.

Proportion Properties (Invertendo & Alternendo)

If two ratios are in proportion (a/b = c/d), then by Invertendo: b/a = d/c, and by Alternendo: a/c = b/d.
